    [1] posting
    ~/

    ❯ posting

    The API client that lives in your terminal.

    An open-source API client with the tools you expect from a desktop app, right in your terminal. Build HTTP, GraphQL, and gRPC requests, inspect responses, and keep your collections in Git alongside your code.

    ~ ❯ brew install darrenburns/homebrew/posting@beta

    Other installation methods

    Read the guide GitHub ↗

    Try a theme.

    [2] keys

    Keyboard first

    features
    1 of 7
    ~ ❯ posting -c atlas-api -e local.env

    Every pane, tab and request gets a label. Type it to go straight there.

    Search every action by name, with its shortcut alongside.

    Inspect and override environment variables, with secrets masked.

    Paste a curl command into the URL bar and press enter to import it.

    Copy a request as curl, with variables resolved.

    Reopen a saved exchange to inspect its response and timing.

    Preview 37 built-in themes, or load your own.

    [3] files

    Your requests are files. Commit them.

    Collections are folders of YAML files: version them in Git and review changes in pull requests.

    Layer .env files with -e and switch environments without restarting. Edits on disk reload automatically.

    shell
    ~ ❯ tree sample-api
sample-api
├── auth
│   ├── login.posting.yaml
│   └── me.posting.yaml
├── cors-preflight.posting.yaml
├── health.posting.yaml
├── local.env
├── staging.env
└── users
    ├── create-user.posting.yaml
    ├── delete-user.posting.yaml
    ├── get-user.posting.yaml
    ├── list-users.posting.yaml
    └── update-user.posting.yaml
2 directories, 11 files

~ ❯ cat sample-api/users/create-user.posting.yaml
name: Create user
description: Create a new user account.
method: POST
url: ${BASE_URL}/users
body:
  content: |-
    {
      "name": "Ada Lovelace",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "role": "admin"
    }
  content_type: application/json
auth:
  type: bearer_token
  bearer_token:
    token: ${API_TOKEN}
headers:
  - name: Content-Type
    value: application/json
    [4] toolkit

    Other features

    autocompletion
    Complete variables with $ in URLs, headers, query, auth and bodies. Header suggestions include descriptions.
    url bar
    Preview the resolved URL before sending. Variables turn green when resolved and red when missing.
    authentication
    Basic, Digest (MD5 and SHA-256) and bearer tokens, with variables allowed in every field.
    responses
    Highlighted JSON, an expandable tree with JSONPath filtering, headers, cookies and a timing trace.
    request tabs
    Keep several requests open, with unsaved changes marked.
    editor & pager
    Press F4 to edit a body in $EDITOR, or F3 to read it in $PAGER.
    keymaps & config
    Rebind actions and configure Posting with config.yaml or POSTING_* environment variables.
    layouts
    Resize panes and arrange the request and response vertically or side by side.
    coding agents
    Let agents send requests through your open Posting session with posting remote. Set it up.
    nerd font icons
    Icons switch on automatically in Ghostty, and anywhere else with one setting.
    [5] upgrade
    posting 2 → 3

    Bring your HTTP collections.

    Posting 3 opens your Posting 2 collections without conversion. Python scripts are preserved but aren't run, history is separate, and some settings and theme options have changed.

    Read the migration guide
    • [ ok ] HTTP requestsno conversion
    • [ ok ] .env filesread unchanged
    • [ ok ] themesmain hex colours
    • [ ok ] keymapssupported actions
    • [ ok ] config.yamlsupported settings
